client_brief:
Aurelian Skin: Aurelian house photography

Project overview
Aurelian Skin is a small clinical skincare line built on eight actives-led products at thirty four to sixty eight dollars. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Aurelian house photography, bottles and actives and Aurelian store tile set, white ground and on-colour.

What we will provide
aurelian_launch_shoot/ (8 frames, 8688 x 5792); aurelian_actives_macros/ (8 frames); aurelian_carton_front.jpg; aurelian_copy.txt; aurelian_reference_page.png; aurelian_speccard_press.pdf. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Additional archive files
aurelian_speccards.csv (8 rows). These files are supplied for provenance only because their former deliverable class is outside this commission. Do not silently turn them into extra scope.

Scope and deliverables
- Aurelian house photography, bottles and actives: Eight bottle masters brought to one clinical target (one white point, one black point, one height in frame) plus a separately targeted family of ingredient close ups, one per launch product with none standing in for two, plus one licensed camera-scale...
- Aurelian store tile set, white ground and on-colour: Eight square store tiles at the retailer's tile size of 2048 x 2048 px on a clean white ground, product optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection, plus eight genuinely transparent variants for the...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,800-$4,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork 'premium clinical skincare brand, logo, label and packaging' launch post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, which asks for a cohesive credible visual identity across the product line plus explicitly 'print-ready files and editable source files', with a stated aesthetic of clean, minimalist, science-driven, premium but not luxurious, strong typography, whitespace and white-background ecommerce imagery. Co-anchor: the Upwork packaging post (cand_64, db_i 271) asking to 'create premium, visually appealing packaging for our beauty and skincare product line' with 'editable source files' among the deliverables. Both real posts name no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Aurelian Skin. The ledger's own repositioning note concedes that from-scratch identity art and free-form layout composition are not connector work; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and an ink-level trace off photographed printed collateral recovers a real mark. So this is that client's actual job: the identity is RECOVERED rather than invented, and the editable source files they asked for are real.

So this is that client's actual job: the identity is RECOVERED rather than invented, and the editable source files they asked for are real.
price_band_and_audience: Prestige-mass clinical actives at 34 to 68 dollars per SKU, buyer 26 to 42 and ingredient literate. The band is load-bearing: at this price the range must sit on a cool near-clinical white, with restrained type, generous white space, no props and no styling that reads as ritual or spa. The same eight products at a 12 dollar mass band would correctly be shot warm, saturated, prop-heavy and tightly cropped to fill the tile, and shipping that treatment here reads downmarket and kills the clinical claim. Push the other way into near-black grounds, extreme sparseness and cosmetic gloss and it becomes a 200 dollar luxury conserve of a skincare line, which misprices a 34 dollar serum. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Clinical skincare and personal care, actives-led, direct to consumer plus specialty retail
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024 in Boston, Massachusetts. A two person founder team, sold for a year to a waiting list and through two dermatology practices before the retail season.
brand_identity.about: Aurelian Skin is a small clinical skincare line built on eight actives-led products at thirty four to sixty eight dollars. In March we open our own online store and enter a specialty chain's twelve doors, so everything a customer sees changes at once. The line is meant to read like a laboratory with good taste: cool, quiet, evidence first, generous with white space and free of decoration. Not a spa, not a discount aisle. Our customer reads the ingredient list before the copy, and the brand is built to reward that: honest claims, clear INCI, restraint in place of ritual.
brand_identity.audience: Women roughly twenty six to forty two, ingredient literate, who research formulations and trust plainness over promise. They shop web stores and specialty beauty floors and judge a product by its panel.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Prestige-mass at thirty four to sixty eight dollars per SKU. Above the mass aisle, below luxury conserve pricing. The middle is the position, and the look must not drift warm and cheap or dark and precious.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained type system for all launch collateral: a clean grotesque for names and body copy carrying the ingredient literacy, with a single quiet display cut for the wordmark. Strong typography and whitespace do the work, no decorative faces.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, factual, unhurried. States what a product does and does not claim. Reads like a well-run lab that respects the reader, never breathless and never coy.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo file was lost when the first designer's drive failed. All that survives is a handheld photograph of an outer carton showing the mark printed in one deep ink: a small-caps lockup set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule. Recovering that mark as usable artwork is part of this engagement. No other source brand files remain.
brand_identity.values: Ingredient honesty, precision in every detail from panel to package, and clinical restraint: at this band, quiet and exact is the brand, and overstatement or gloss would undercut the claim.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_launch_shoot/ (8 frames, 8688 x 5792)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography shot in-house by a friend across three afternoons, one SKU per frame, pale sweep, fifty megapixel body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All eight, same sweep, same corner of her studio. Some read cooler than others and one is brighter, but they are good pictures."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frames are far larger than anything downstream expects, and the one-call background knockout silently reduces oversized inputs and reports it in no message and no error, only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object with output dimensions below source dimensions. The returned cutout is clean, complete and correct looking at preview scale; the shortfall only appears when the square store tile is cut from it, and by then the only route back to the retailer's tile size is interpolation, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while saying so only inside its own tradeoffs. Separately the 30ml frosted-glass SKU sits at almost the luminance of the sweep at its shoulder, so subject detection has no contrast there and hands back a soft rim on that frame alone.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_actives_macros/ (8 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Macro close ups of the raw actives themselves, shot on a later day: a drop on glass, a pipette tip, a crystal, a powder cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ingredient close ups for the product pages. Tighter, different day."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Each frame is a single small element on a near empty ground. A subject-focused crop on that kind of art returns a confident looking result at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a detection bounding box buried in the metadata, and on sparse art it can lock onto a specular highlight or a reflection instead of the subject and hand back a crop that clips most of it, at full success. Which of the eight this happens to is a property of each frame's own contrast. Separately there are eight macros for eight products but two of them are the same active shot twice and one launch product has no macro at all, which no filename or column reveals.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_carton_front.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of an outer carton standing on a bench, the mark printed in one deep ink on pale board: a compound lockup of small-caps type set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists. We lost the file when the drive failed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup on a photographed substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the substrate returns the carton rather than the ink; a compound prompt returns the type ring and silently drops the monogram and the hairline rule while looking entirely plausible; and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The ink and the board also run close in value on the shadowed right third of the carton face.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the eight product names, their INCI lines, the claims cleared by their regulatory reviewer, and the launch prices.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as approved. The INCI lines cannot be edited."

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_reference_page.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of a store page layout the founders like, from a category-neutral retailer, supplied as a proportion reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly how much room we want the product to have."

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_speccard_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press PDF the specialty chain's print vendor supplied as the template each per-SKU shelf-edge and tester-station card is struck from: an A6 portrait card carrying the product name, an ingredients (INCI) block, the cleared claim, the price and a square product-image well, 3mm bleed present, fonts embedded.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The chain's card template. Every SKU gets one of these on the shelf edge and at the tester station, so their printer wants a run built off this file. The INCI on it is the approved line and cannot change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as five tidy blocks, but the product name, the INCI block and the cleared claim are set as ONE continuous threaded story flowing through three linked frames, so the INCI is an offset inside a continuous flow rather than an addressable field. The mapping readout normalises and shortens that story, so an offset computed from the readout silently drops or misplaces the INCI while validation returns valid and both preparation and render report success; the only evidence the INCI landed is reading the rendered card. The square image well IS a real bindable graphic frame, and a 3mm bleed box IS present in the source PDF; but convert_pdf_to_indd collapses it, setting the converted document's BleedBox equal to its TrimBox, so the connector cannot carry bleed through a PDF-derived merge template and the honest deliverable is trim-only.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_speccards.csv (8 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The per-SKU card data the chain wants merged: one row per launch product carrying the product name, its locked INCI line, its cleared claim, its price and a picture reference, derived from the approved copy.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One row per product for the shelf cards. The INCI lines are the approved ones and cannot be edited."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Prices are written inconsistently across the eight rows, dollar sign on some, two decimals on some, bare integers on others, so a naive bind prints mixed formats on a clinical line. The frosted SKU's name carries the internal warehouse parenthetical '(30ml frosted)' that must be kept off the retail card. And the picture column carries an off-by-one copy-down slip on the exfoliating toner row, which points at the cleanser frame rather than the toner's own, so a merge that trusts the column shows the wrong bottle on that card. The INCI and claim cells are comma-bearing and quoted, and none of this is revealed by any header.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one-call knockout gives back a picture the store tile can still be cut from. The captures are 8688 x 5792 and the knockout silently reduces oversized inputs, reporting it in no message, no warning and no error: the only trace is a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object with output dimensions below source dimensions. Nothing in the tool's description mentions a size ceiling and nothing states where it sits. The returned cutout is clean, complete and correct at preview scale. The shortfall appears only when the square tile is cut, and the only route back to the retailer's size is interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a two times cap while reporting it solely inside its own tradeoffs.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. The defensible order is straighten, grade, knock out at source scale, then choose the crop, precisely so the crop is chosen after the cut edge is visible; there is no read-ahead for the ceiling and no parameter that controls it. An agent that cropped first would be trading away crop choice for a reason nobody has told it. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for square store pictures and says nothing about resolution; the no-enlargement line in the acceptance bar is the client's standing trade requirement, not a disclosure that a tool shrinks things. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different route, decided per frame: crop to the subject's own bounds at native scale so the knockout receives a frame under the ceiling, or abandon the one-call knockout for a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled to white.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route for all eight frames, re-derive every white-ground plate and every transparent variant through the new route, and re-read both the downscaled and the upscale entries in every returned tradeoffs object before any tile is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight store tiles that are either short of the retailer's required size and bounced at upload, or brought to size by interpolation and shipped soft, on a clinical line whose entire claim is precision.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the launch look is built on. The client asked for the bottles to sit on a surface with a soft shadow rather than float. Authored the natural way that is a blurred element or a layered shadow, and the importer discards a blur filter outright and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, with no warning and a successful response. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the square and tall canvases can be checked no other way. Whether what survives still reads as a bottle sitting on a surface, or as a bottle floating beside a grey smudge, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a look, and the acceptance line about sitting rather than floating is the client's own art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a DIFFERENT upstream asset, a bottle composited onto a solid house ground in a single knockout call so the ground is part of the raster, or to reduce the shadow to the single layer the importer keeps and re-judge whether it still reads, and then re-compose the canvas around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the launch masters through a different knockout route or re-cast the shadow as the single surviving layer, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A launch set delivered as an editable file in which the bottles float on flat white on the two canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a subject-aware crop can find the subject in the ingredient close ups at all. Those frames are one small element on a near empty ground. The crop tool answers a subject-focused request on that kind of art with a confident looking result at a plausible size and reports its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a detection bounding box buried in the metadata; on sparse art it can lock onto a specular highlight or a reflection and return a crop that clips most of the subject, at full success. Which of the eight this happens to is a property of each frame's own contrast and is not visible by looking at the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it. The safe route, an explicit selection with a returned bounding box driving a bounds crop, costs three calls per frame and is what a competent agent adopts once the cheap route has been seen to fail. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the macros are tighter and were shot on a different day. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected frames go through a different chain, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the detection confidence and bounds on every macro crop, and for each frame below a defensible threshold re-do the crop through an explicit selection of the material by its own visual properties, a returned bounding box and a padded bounds crop, then inspect each result rather than the response.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ingredient panels showing a third of a droplet and the edge of a pipette, on a line whose customer buys on ingredient literacy and reads that panel before the copy.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Whether the eight bottle frames are one shoot. The client believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the two off-rig frames before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Knockout route per frame: the one-call route for coherent opaque bottles versus a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled for the frosted SKU whose shoulder has no contrast.
Whether to trust a confident looking crop on sparse macro art or to spend three calls per frame on an explicit selection.
Whether eight macro files for eight products is eight actives, and how to say so when it is not.
Which mark variant carries the launch canvases, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at full canvas.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a clinical band and an ingredient-literate reader, plus the real numeric weight per family.

acceptance_snapshot: All eight store tiles sit on a clean white ground, square at the retailer's tile size of 2048 x 2048 px, the bottle optically centred with nothing touching the edge, and the cut edge holds when looked at close up rather than at preview scale.

The eight bottles read as ONE range when laid in a row as a store page lays them: one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
In the launch pictures the bottles read as sitting on a surface rather than floating, on every canvas and not only the first one.

The retail shelf-card run produces one card per SKU with that SKU's own locked INCI line present and correct, its cleared claim and its price, page count equalling the eight-SKU record count, each card binding its own bottle picture, prices normalised to one format, and the frosted SKU's internal warehouse note kept off the retail name.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop's returned tradeoff report carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of skincare bottles. IDENTITY: these are this line's actual eight products with their actual labels and their actual regulatory-cleared claims, and the mark must be RECOVERED off a photographed carton rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different company's logo. SPEC: the retailer needs eight square tiles at an exact size with nothing touching the edge and no interpolated pixels, plus transparent variants for their own coloured band, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the launch set is defined by being editable, since the date and the featured product will move and the founders explicitly cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this knockout come back smaller than it went in, does this crop actually contain the droplet, did the shadow survive the import, and did this rendered shelf card actually carry this SKU's own locked INCI line. And the retail shelf cards are a per-SKU data merge that must bind each card to its own SKU's locked INCI line, cleared claim and price at print resolution with page count equal to record count, which a generated picture of a card neither produces nor can be checked for.
